CONTENTS
MS LUCY LETBY (continued)
Cross-examination by MR JOHNSON (continued)
Friday, 19 May 2023
(In the absence of the jury)
Yes, Mr Myers.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: May it please you, my Lord, there's one matter I'd be grateful to raise before we continue today. It won't take long. It's just a concern, so I raise it now in this way before we proceed, coming out of one aspect of the cross-examination of Ms Letby yesterday relating to [Baby C].
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: For your Lordship's note and anyone's reference, it's the passage in the transcript between pages 129 to 135. It was relating to Ms Letby's assessment of the condition of [Baby C] and it began with the question:
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: "Do you accept that [Baby C] progressed well having been born in good condition?"
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: And the aim, the purpose of it, which was dealt with part-way through, was the question, "It all paints parents a positive picture", to which she assented.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: That question was not based just upon matters relating to her experience, but more generally. We appreciate the task faced by the prosecution, as it is by us, in fact, in traversing the evidence in this case in a practicable way. But what happened over about four pages of transcript and a couple of minutes of court time was a fairly swift survey of the component parts of a week of evidence, much of which Ms Letby had no particular involvement with, in fact all of it, concluding with a swift assessment or statement, rather, of the view of Dr Marnerides that there was no bowel obstruction, simply put like that. It was said:
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: "You'll remember he said there was no bowel obstruction or words to that effect. The histology did not show he had any bowel issue?"
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: And Ms Letby said yes and that was that.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: That is a matter that is hotly contested and on which there is a lot of evidence competing. Our concern is that it is one thing for her involvement to form the basis of questioning like that. It certainly isn't, with respect, we submit, appropriate for her to engage really in what becomes the provision of an expert opinion, which is what happens once we get into the territory of inviting her to comment on expert evidence, or putting it to her, putting it before the jury, of course, and one part of the expert evidence before the jury, as a statement.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: I have raised the matter with my learned friend Mr Johnson King's Counsel and he will respond as he sees fit, but we would say it is not an approach that we have taken with other witnesses and certainly we have not embarked upon rehearsing pieces of expert evidence with non-experts for them to comment upon as if they are experts or expect them to do so.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: So our principal concern is treating Ms Letby as, in effect, a surrogate expert on what are key issues of expert evidence, ultimately, which draw upon a careful analysis of what has been sometimes days, if not a week, of evidence.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: There is a subsidiary issue, we respectfully observe, to be borne in mind: given her circumstances as a witness in this case, it is a task and a half for her to absorb a mass of detail at speed, putting up different charts or nursing notes on the system that she then has to look at and is asked questions like, "Do you agree with what..." or, "Just have a read of the rest of that, what do you think", or picking out one side of the IC cares chart that has breathing support but not assisting her by identifying the repeated references to bile aspirates that run through it.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: It's a matter for Ms Letby to read carefully what is put in front of her so far as she can. That is for her.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: But our concern is she is assisted with relevant details so far as possible. I say that recognising, as I'm bound to from what I have been dealing with, the task Mr Johnson is dealing with.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: So I don't say this as any type of slight or criticism, but as a matter of caution, to bear in mind the defendant's position, but over and above that we would ask that she not be invited to, in effect, become a surrogate expert on matters that go beyond what she or any other nurse has been expected to deal with in the case. We know there are general matters of nursing practice that she will be asked about but when we get down to questions of, for example, bowel issues from the evidence of Dr Marnerides, it's important, we submit, that she not be drawn into that and it's for that reason that we just raise that as carefully and respectfully as we can, my Lord.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Thank you, Mr Myers.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Mr Johnson.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: There are a number of issues there, my Lord.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: The first is the speed of the cross-examination. I have repeatedly said to the witness that if she needs more time to read a document then of course she shall have it.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: And you will continue to do that. If I think you are forcing something at too quick a pace, I will intervene. So I will be alert to the point that Mr Myers is making and if I think you are in any way being inappropriate or too quick or too selective in relation to matters, I will intervene.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes. The second is selection. My learned friend, unsurprisingly, in chief was very selective --
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Well, I'm not overly impressed because the -- I understand the point that Mr Myers is making, but throughout this case there have been, as there always are -- one side is particularly selective in relation to certain pieces of evidence and perhaps passes over other pieces of evidence. But if you -what I will simply say, Mr Myers, is if you consider, in relation to any particular line of questioning, it is unfairly selective and presents an inaccurate picture of the clinical situation at that time, then you should raise it. If I think it does, I will, but otherwise -- which is no more than common practice. We'll do it that way.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Finally, the surrogate expert witness point.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: I don't accept that as a criticism at all, my Lord. An example of the way it was articulated to me was that it was not acceptable to be referring the witness to notes or opinions of other people and asking her to comment.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: There are two issues here. The first is that my learned friend repeatedly, and I am not complaining about this, but repeatedly set the scene in each case.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: And we have a record of the times between when my learned friend started talking in each case and the time that he first asked questions.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: I know. I think what I will say in relation to this issue is that you are certainly not precluded from drawing the witness's attention, the defendant's attention, to unchallenged expert evidence conclusions --
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: -- and then asking questions about that.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: You certainly are not precluded from doing that. But if it is a controversial expert opinion then it may be more difficult. Obviously, she can't give clinical evidence.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: She has, as is evident from her evidence, a wealth of experience despite her relatively short period of nursing and a lot of knowledge about medical matters, but you'll know where the boundary is and if I think you're going over the boundary, Mr Johnson, I will intervene. Otherwise, we'll leave that. All right, Mr Myers?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: I'm grateful, my Lord, thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: I hope that's clarified the ground rules.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes, thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Good. Thank you very much. The usual situation: choose an appropriate moment after an hour or so.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Certainly.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Thank you very much.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Jury in, please.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: (In the presence of the jury)
Good morning, members of the jury. I'm sorry we are late coming in, I was just dealing with a matter. We're in a position to proceed now. Sorry about that delay.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

Cross-examination by MR JOHNSON (continued)
Yesterday at the end of the day, we'd got to the position in the chronology or the sequence of events relating to [Baby C] just before he collapsed at 23.15; do you remember that?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: I had just been asking you about a part of your interview; do you remember that?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And I was asking you, as well as the part of your interview, about some text messages that you had sent to your friend, Jennifer Jones-Key.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Just to put us back into the sequence, the text messages were sent at between 23.01 and 23.09. They're between tiles 174 and 180. Okay?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: I was asking you questions specifically about what I was suggesting to you was your acceptance that at the time, this is in interview, your acceptance in interview that at the time [Baby C] collapsed, you were in nursery 1. Do you remember that?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And do you accept that you were in nursery 1 at the time [Baby C] collapsed?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Why did you tell the police that you did accept it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Based on what Sophie Ellis saw and what was told to me, I took that to be accurate. I have no memory of being in the room.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: If you have no memory, how can you dispute?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I dispute the fact that I have not agreed that I was definitely in the nursery.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: I'll put the question a different way then. Are you disputing that you were in the room at the time [Baby C] collapsed?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, I have no recollection of that.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Well, I'm going to suggest to you -- I'm not going to do this every time because otherwise we'll be here a long time, but I'm going to suggest to you that you're ignoring the question and in due course I may suggest to the jury that the reason you're ignoring the question is because you can't answer the question. All right? So I'll give you one more opportunity to answer it.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Do you dispute that you were in the room at the time [Baby C] collapsed?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Why?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Because I have no memory of that.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you remember being born?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you dispute that you were born?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Just before the prosecution say that you were in the room with [Baby C] when he collapsed, you were texting Jennifer Jones-Key.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: You had left one of your babies in the nursery, having just taken his or her observations; do you remember that?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I can't say when I left that baby, no. I don't know where I did the texting.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Well, let's just look at this if we can, please. Can you go to the neonatal review at page 3 of 9? Can you see there at line 65 the fact that you took the observations of the baby PE?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And PE was in nursery 3, wasn't she?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you remember PE as a matter of interest?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Can you see what's in the line above that?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, Nicola Dennison has made an entry on the fluid balance chart.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes. Just to remind us, who is Nicola Dennison?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: The band 4 nursery nurse.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Why did you leave PE with Nicola Dennison?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I haven't handed over care to Nicola Dennison.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: No, but whether or not you've handed over care, why did you leave a nursery nurse, a band 4, someone of lesser qualification to you, with a nursery nurse (sic)?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Well, I can't answer that. It's not unusual for nursery nurses to help out with feeds.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Well, it may not be, but I'm asking why you left that child at that time with that nursery nurse.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I have no memory of that.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Whose responsibility was PE?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Mine.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Did you have something better to do?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No. Both babies that night had the care they needed.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: That's not the question. I'm not suggesting that Nicola Dennison couldn't do what you left her to do.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: What I'm asking you is why you left her to do it.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I can't recall that now.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Well, I will remind you. Can we go to tile 174? To moan to Jennifer Jones-Key is the answer, isn't it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Sorry?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, I've not left somebody to go to text. I've also been doing things with JE as well at that time.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Oh, show us on the neonatal review, please, what you were doing with JE.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Where's that?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Lines 55 and 56.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Right. Yes. Okay. But we know that that time is the wrong time, don't we?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: It's not a wrong time, it's an approximation.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Sorry, could we go back to the text, please? According to your evidence that you gave to the jury, you never use your phone in a clinical area.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, that's right.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So you were not in the nursery at 23.01, were you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: If you hadn't been texting your mate, would you have had time to feed JE -- sorry, PE?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I did feed JE at that same time, which is possibly why Nurse Dennison looked after PE for me.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Would you answer the question, please? If you hadn't been texting your mate, would you have had time to feed PE?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I can't answer that.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Because you were texting Jennifer Jones-Key right up to 23.09, weren't you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Eight minutes. That might well have been long enough to feed your baby, mightn't it --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: -- PE?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I can't recall the circumstances around that now.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: But it took you out of the nursery, didn't it, whatever the circumstances were?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, I would not have used my phone at the cot side, so yes, I would have been in the doorway or elsewhere on the unit, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: This is the time we suggest that you were in nursery 1 with [Baby C]; yes?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I don't accept that, no.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Mel Taylor wasn't in the room when [Baby C] collapsed, was she?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I don't recall her evidence.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Well, that's her evidence and if we look at tile 185, please:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Called to help baby. When arrived to baby, baby apnoeic."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: She told us she wasn't in the nursery, didn't she?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I can't remember her saying that, but she is saying she's come over to the baby, yes, to the baby's cot side. She doesn't specify being out of the nursery.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: That was her evidence.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay. I can't recall her evidence right here, right now.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you remember how Mel described you --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: -- at this time? "Cool and calm"; do you dispute that?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, I would expect members of staff to be cool and calm on a unit. That's what we're trained to do.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And you said to Sophie Ellis:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "He's just had a brady and a desat."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I can't recall saying that.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you dispute that you said it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I have no memory of saying it.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Well, I'll ask you one more time: do you dispute that you said it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, because I have no memory of that.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you remember the arrival of Dr Katherine Davis at 23.26?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, not specifically. I remember doctors arriving but I couldn't be specific on times, no.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Can we go to tile 187, please. This is Dr Davis' -- I think this is the wrong tile, actually, for the note.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Sorry, no, it isn't, sorry. My fault:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "23.26, crash bleeped to attend NICU. On arrival, Guedel airway in situ, bagged via Neopuff by nursing staff. Occasional intermittent gasps noted. Chest compressions commenced."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Can we scroll down, please?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I think actually, going back up -- sorry to be pedantic about this, but I am a pedant -- it says:
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: "Bagged via Neopuff by nursing staff. Chest compressions in progress on arrival."
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Sorry, yes.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: And then "chest compressions recommenced"
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: three lines further down.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes, quite right. I was just trying to -- if Mr Myers thinks I'm missing anything out, I'm sure he will --
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: It's not Mr Myers, it's me. I'm just reading what we can all see on the note.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes. We can see the condition of [Baby C] there:
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Occasional intermittent gasps."
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Is that right?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Is that what you saw, for example, with [Baby I] on 13 -- I can't remember which month it was now. 13/10, wasn't it, 2015?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I'm not sure that's that date, is it, for [Baby I]?
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: I think it was the second incident, 13 October. Anyway.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: You know the incident I'm talking about in nursery 2?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: The same sort of thing, is it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And then if we can scroll down, please. We have the two attempts at intubation, but:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Unable to pass ETT as cords ++. Clear oral secretions, no blood seen. Neopuffed with Guedel airway."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Cords ++. She told us, Dr Davies, that they were swollen and oedematous, was the word she used. What does oedematous mean?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Swollen.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Had you put something down [Baby C]'s throat?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you agree that this becomes a theme of some of these collapses, that when the doctors look down the throats of these children, they see either swelling or bleeding?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, I know other doctors have commented on that, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes. This is not something that's caused by the use of a Guedel airway, is it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I can't answer that.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: There then ensued a very long and protracted decline for [Baby C], didn't there?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And [Baby C] had massive gastric dilation and ballooning of the stomach, didn't he?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: At this point?
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Well, that's the evidence of what was found after the event.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yesterday I was asking you about Sophie Ellis having aspirated [Baby C]'s stomach just before she fed him that one half of 1ml of milk --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: -- at 11 o'clock. Do you agree that something caused [Baby C]'s stomach and bowel to dilate between 11 o'clock and his collapse?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So the air you're referring to is before the collapse?
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: That's what's found after he died. We're suggesting that's the reason for the collapse.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I think if he was found with air when he's died, that could be related to the Neopuff resuscitation. I'm not accepting that he had noticeable gas between 23.00 and 23.15.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So something caused him to -- he was fed at 23.00?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Something caused him to collapse at 23.15?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Extensive CPR was undertaken?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: For some reason, a heart rate was restored; do you remember that?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And he clung to life for a further 5 hours plus?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Had you ever seen that sort of a decline before?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: In the context of when he first collapsed?
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, I've seen babies suddenly collapse before, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And cling to life the way [Baby C] did?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, I haven't seen that before, no.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: You enjoyed the aftermath of this, didn't you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Why were you so keen to involve yourself with the [Family of Baby C] as they cradled their dying son?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I don't agree with that. I don't recall being there for a lot of the time like they've said.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you remember [Nurse B] said that she had to keep pulling you out of the family room?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: That was not disputed on your behalf with her, was it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I can't recall that now.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you dispute it now?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That I'd been in the family room?
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Repeatedly.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, I agree that I've probably gone round at some point but not repeatedly, no. I don't recall [Nurse B] having to pull me back out.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: What she said was this:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "I asked Lucy to focus back in nursery 3 on baby JE because I was still heavily concerned about him. However, Lucy went into the family room a few times and I asked her to come out and to leave that family [that is the [Family of Baby C]] with Mel."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Are you disputing that?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Of course, Mel is senior to you, isn't she?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: More experienced?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Given that Mel was looking after this family, what useful function were you performing?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I -- I don't understand the question, sorry.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: What were you contributing --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I can't recall from --
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: -- to the dreadful situation that the [Family of Baby C] were going through?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I can't recall whether I assisted Mel with any of the mementos, which is a two-person job.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: You can't recall it, so what, are you disputing that you did assist her?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON
